Read the predictions of other classifiers

Source: R/read_classifier_output.R
read_classifier_output.Rd

Reads the prediction files of classifiers other than BirdNET and returns them in the shape of read_selection_tables(), so that they can go to select_clips(), select_directed(), threshold_history(), export_occupancy_data() and score_detections().

Usage

read_classifier_output(
  files,
  format = c("perch", "opensoundscape", "arbimon"),
  score_scale = NULL,
  min_confidence = 0.1,
  site_pattern = NULL,
  audio_root = NULL,
  window_s = 5,
  recordings = NULL,
  label = NULL
)

Arguments

files

Character vector of paths to prediction files (CSV), or to folders searched recursively for .csv files.

format

Character scalar, one of "perch", "opensoundscape" or "arbimon".

score_scale

NULL or character scalar, one of "logit" or "probability": the scale of the scores in the files. NULL takes "logit" for Perch and OpenSoundscape and "probability" for Arbimon.

min_confidence

Numeric scalar in [0, 1]. Rows with a lower confidence are left out.

site_pattern

NULL or character scalar, regular expression with one capture group that takes the site from the name of the audio file, as in read_selection_tables(). NULL takes the folder of the audio file.

audio_root

NULL or character scalar, folder that relative audio paths are resolved against (for Perch, the folder the embeddings were computed from). Absolute paths and URLs are kept as they are.

window_s

Numeric scalar > 0, length of the window in seconds, used for the Perch files that do not store its end.

recordings

NULL, a data frame or a character scalar path to the recordings table of an Arbimon project backup, with the columns recording_id and meta (JSON with the original filename) or filename. Needed for the Arbimon "export all" files only.

label

NULL or character scalar, the species of an Arbimon "export all" file (one job, one template). Needed for those files only.

Value

A tibble with one row per prediction: site, begin_time, end_time, species_code, confidence, begin_path and file_offset (the columns required by select_clips()), plus label, score (as in the file) and classifier; for Arbimon, also verdict.

Formats

"perch": the inference CSV of Perch, written by write_inference_csv() of perch-hoplite (perch_hoplite.agile.classifier) or of the earlier perch repository (chirp.inference.classify). One row per window and label whose logit exceeds the threshold chosen when the file was written. Three headers are recognised:

HeaderWriter
idx,project,filename,window_start,window_end,label,logitsperch-hoplite, from December 2025
idx,dataset_name,source_id,offset,label,logitsperch-hoplite, 2025
filename, timestamp_s, label, logitperch (chirp)

The file of the audio (filename or source_id) is relative to the folder the embeddings were computed from: give that folder in audio_root. The two older headers do not store the end of the window, which is taken as the start plus window_s seconds (5 s, the window of the Perch models).

"opensoundscape": the table returned by predict() of an OpenSoundscape model (CNN or the models of the bioacoustics model zoo, e.g. BirdNET and Perch) and saved with to_csv(): the columns file, start_time and end_time, then one column of scores per class. Windows whose scores are missing (audio that could not be read) are left out.

"arbimon": the results of a pattern matching job of Arbimon (template matching; the score is a correlation between 0 and 1). Two exports are recognised:

  • the download of one job, with the columns recording (the name of the audio file), site, species, songtype, x1, x2 (start and end of the match, in seconds from the start of the recording), validated and score; older exports name the minute column min and lack frequency, and both variants are read;

  • the "export all results" of a project, one file per job, with the columns x1, x2, score, validated, site_name, recording_id and audio_url. It names neither the species nor the audio file: give the species in label and the recordings table of a project backup (recordings.0001.csv), whose meta column holds the original file name of each recording. Files without any result (empty files) are skipped.

The site is the Arbimon site (site or site_name) unless site_pattern is given. The label is the species; a species with more than one song type gets the song type in brackets ("Coccyzus minor (Simple Call)"). The reviews done in Arbimon are kept in verdict: present (or 1) is "positive", not present is "negative", and (not validated), empty or 0 is missing. The "export all" files hold only 1 and 0, and whether 0 marks a rejected or an unreviewed match is not documented, so a 0 is read as missing.

Scores

sheepdog works with scores between 0 and 1, as BirdNET writes them. Perch writes logits, and OpenSoundscape returns logits unless predict() was called with activation_layer = "sigmoid" or "softmax". Neither file records the scale, so it is given in score_scale: with "logit" (the default of both classifiers), confidence is the logistic function of the score, plogis(score); with "probability", the score is used as it is and must lie between 0 and 1. The calibration models work on the logit of confidence, which for logits is the score itself, so no information is lost. The original score is kept in score.

Arbimon correlations lie between 0 and 1 and are read as they are (score_scale = "probability", its default), although they are not probabilities.

Rows with confidence below min_confidence are left out (0.1, the default minimum confidence of BirdNET). A Perch file already lacks the windows below the logit threshold used to write it; a logit of 0 is a confidence of 0.5.

Sites and labels

For Perch and OpenSoundscape, the site is the folder that holds each audio file (site_A/rec.wav gives site_A), or is taken from the file name with site_pattern, as in read_selection_tables(). The date and hour of a recording are read from its file name (YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS) by the functions downstream, as for BirdNET.

sheepdog names the folder of a species after the part of species_code after the last underscore. Labels of other classifiers are names or codes without that part, so species_code is built as the label and its lower-case form with every run of other characters replaced by a hyphen: "Boana raniceps" gives "Boana raniceps_boana-raniceps", whose folder is boana_raniceps. The label is kept in label.

References

Ghani, B., Denton, T., Kahl, S. and Klinck, H. (2023). Global birdsong embeddings enable superior transfer learning for bioacoustic classification. Scientific Reports, 13, 22876. doi:10.1038/s41598-023-49989-z

Lapp, S., Rhinehart, T., Freeland-Haynes, L., Khilnani, J., Syunkova, A. and Kitzes, J. (2023). OpenSoundscape: an open-source bioacoustics analysis package for Python. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 14(9), 2321-2328. doi:10.1111/2041-210X.14196

Aide, T. M., Corrada-Bravo, C., Campos-Cerqueira, M., Milan, C., Vega, G. and Alvarez, R. (2013). Real-time bioacoustics monitoring and automated species identification. PeerJ, 1, e103. doi:10.7717/peerj.103

See also

read_selection_tables() for BirdNET, read_pamdp() for pamDP data packages.
